test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Stars appear to twinkle in the night sky because ______.

options.text: Light from stars undergoes atmospheric refraction
The distance between stars and Earth keeps varying
Stars move rapidly in the sky

solution:
The correct answer is __**Light from stars undergoes atmospheric refraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The twinkling of a star is due to the **atmospheric refraction** of star light. As the light from a star enters the **Earth’s atmosphere**, it undergoes **refraction** continuously before it reaches the **Earth**.
 
• Since the stars are very distant, they approximate **point-sized sources** of light. As the path of rays of light coming from the star goes on varying slightly, the **apparent position** of the star fluctuates and the amount of **starlight** entering the eye flickers. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **atmospheric refraction** occurs in a medium of gradually changing **refractive index**. The **Earth’s atmosphere** is not stationary; its **density** and **temperature** change continuously, leading to changes in the **refractive index** of different layers of air.
 
• While stars may have intrinsic variability, the "twinkling" we observe is primarily an **optical illusion** caused by the atmosphere rather than the stars changing their **brightness** continuously. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **distance** between stars and Earth is vast, and any minor **orbital movement** or **variation in distance** is too insignificant to cause the rapid flickering effect known as twinkling. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Although stars do move at high **velocities**, their **proper motion** is not perceivable over short timeframes to the naked eye and does not cause the twinkling effect. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Why Planets do not Twinkle:** 
 
 
• Unlike stars, **planets** are much closer to the **Earth** and are thus seen as **extended sources** (a collection of many point-sized sources) rather than a single **point source**.
 
• The total variation in the amount of light entering our eye from all the individual **point-sized sources** in a planet will average out to **zero**, thereby **nullifying** the twinkling effect.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Refraction Phenomena:**
 
 
• **Advance Sunrise and Delayed Sunset:** The **Sun** is visible to us about **2 minutes** before the actual sunrise and about **2 minutes** after the actual sunset because of **atmospheric refraction**.
 
• **Apparent Position:** Due to the bending of light, stars appear slightly **higher** (above their actual position) when viewed near the **horizon**.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index:** The **refractive index** of the atmosphere generally increases as we move closer to the **Earth's surface** because the air becomes **denser**. This causes the light to bend toward the **normal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scintillation:** This is the scientific term for the **twinkling** of stars. It is caused by **small-scale fluctuations** in the **air density** resulting from **turbulence** in the **atmosphere**.
 
• **Astronomy:** To avoid the blurring and twinkling caused by the **atmosphere**, modern large **telescopes** (like the **Hubble Space Telescope**) are placed in **outer space**, or use **adaptive optics** to cancel out the atmospheric distortion.
 
• **Medium Consistency:** If the **Earth** had no **atmosphere**, stars would not twinkle and would appear as steady **points of light** against a **black sky**.

7f
